campus_notes: Purdue University Residences publishes exact room dimensions (width x length, occasionally ceiling height) and closet dimensions for the illustrated room layouts on each hall page, with the caveat that illustrations are approximate. The official rates data (CSV behind the housing-rates page) provides the full 2026-27 room-type inventory per building with academic-year rates, capacity, AC, and bath flags - it is far more granular than the illustrated layouts, so many rate tiers carry no dimensions; dimension layouts are attached to rate tiers only where the mapping is unambiguous, and ambiguities are noted on the affected rooms. Rates shown are per person per ACADEMIC YEAR (not per semester), utilities included. Standard mattress is 77" x 36" (Twin XL 80" in the newest halls, e.g. the Parker halls; 89" long mattress on request for residents 6'4"+); most beds can be lofted (Bedloft.com rentals in some halls). Purdue Indianapolis buildings (North Hall, LUX on Capitol) are excluded. Master-leased apartment properties (Aspire, Fuse, etc.) appear with rate-only rooms; Hilltop and Provenance also publish dimensions/square footage.

dorms.notes: Cary Quadrangle is one of Purdue University's historic all-male residence halls, offering a unique blend of tradition and modern comfort. While Cary is the oldest hall on campus, its four outer buildings, West, Northwest, Northeast, and East, were fully renovated in 2007. These updates introduced air-conditioned double-suite-style rooms, where two rooms share a private connecting bathroom. The South building preserves its original layout, providing a variety of non-air-conditioned room types, including singles, doubles, triples, and quads. These rooms feature community-style restrooms located throughout each floor, fostering a classic residence hall experience.

dorms.notes: Earhart Hall offers traditional-style rooms with shared community bathrooms. Each room is air-conditioned with individual temperature controls for comfort year-round. The hall features inviting community spaces including a shared kitchen, private study rooms, and large social lounges, perfect for relaxing, collaborating, or connecting with friends. Best of all, Earhart Dining Court is located right downstairs, so you can grab a meal without stepping outside, especially convenient during Indiana’s chilly winters. For busy days, the “On-The-GO!” station offers quick, hot or cold meal options to keep you fueled and focused.

dorms.notes: Hillenbrand Hall offers suite-style living in a modern, spacious environment where two suites share a bathroom. The hall blends contemporary design with traditional comfort, creating a quiet and relaxed atmosphere ideal for academic success and personal growth. Residents enjoy convenient access to Hillenbrand Dining Court located on the ground floor, along with study spaces, laundry facilities, and leadership opportunities through hall organizations. As home to The Data Mine learning community, Hillenbrand supports students from all majors in developing data literacy and collaborative research skills. Its central location and vibrant residential culture make it a dynamic place to live, learn, and connect.
